facts.text: Fairmont City first appeared in 1910 when the Pennsylvania Railroad built a roundhouse here, marking the townsite's birth.
A zinc smelter opened in 1912, and after primary smelting ended in 1953, the plant closed completely in 1967.
In 2017, Fairmont City Library earned International Grand Prize First Place for Library‑Community Interaction, beating Kansas City and Catawba County libraries.
Fairmont City sits atop portions of the Cahokia Mounds, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that dates back to the pre‑Columbian era.
Mexican community leaders founded the Mexican‑American Society of Fairmont City around 1940 to support newcomers and foster social opportunities.
In April 2016, the EPA listed Fairmont City's former zinc plant on the National Priorities List after finding high levels of lead, arsenic, cadmium, and zinc in soil.
